assessments.reasoning: The official SAP Release 754 glossary defines CDS DCL as the data control language of ABAP CDS and ties it to defining CDS objects in DCL source code in access control.

The SAP Release 754 ABAP CDS in ABAP Dictionary topic expressly distinguishes the CDS DDL and CDS DCL languages used in the technology, singles out CDS DDL for data definitions, and distinguishes the HANA CDS variant. This supports the claim’s boundary in the same backend edition.

SAP’s ADT client guide cover dates version 3.16. In section 3.3.1 on page 75 it assigns access controls to DCL, and page 108 describes DCL authorizations separately from data definitions and DDL. The guide provides functional context across its stated editorial scope, while the 7.54 glossary controls the exact edition claim.

challenge.method: Challenge the identity by comparing the glossary with the full technology overview, the DDL definition workflow, the separate DCL role source, the ADT client guide, and the Linguist category and samples. Test a merge with HANA CDS, CDS DDL, the umbrella technology, or classic authorization roles.
challenge.results: SAP explicitly places DCL inside ABAP CDS and assigns it its own access-control source. The DDL workflow and .asddls examples assign data definitions to DDL, and the SAP overview distinguishes HANA CDS. SAP identifies classic authorization as a related mechanism and separately describes the CDS role. None of these alternatives is an identity match for ABAP CDS DCL.

limitations: The entity denotes ABAP CDS DCL in the documented SAP scope. ABAP CDS technology, CDS DDL, HANA CDS and classic authorization roles each have their own boundaries.
